content:
incident-bot: 🔔 PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-runtime-eu (high request error rate) and service=redwood-runtime-us-east (heartbeat loss) — multiple pages, see <https://pagerduty.example/alerts|alerts>

Alex P: acked pagerduty. i'm on it. looking at router metrics now.

Jordan K: seeing a short spike in 5xxs from the eu pool around 1719001180, followed by a gap. could be transient backend flake. no sustained tail.

Maya R: @Alex P @Jordan K are there matching autoscale events or infra events? autoscaler logs?

Alex P: checking autoscaler — there was a rapid scale-up attempt at 1719001205 but it finished quickly. Logs:
```
2026-03-14T20:20:05Z autoscaler: scale_up request id=abc123 target=+2 GPUs
2026-03-14T20:20:34Z autoscaler: scale_up complete id=abc123
```

Emily S: customer-facing telemetry (ingress success rate) shows a tiny blip (~0.6% impacted requests) during the spike. No open support tickets yet.

Jordan K: also seeing duplicate alerts from incident-bot — looks like cross-region routing sent the same symptom to two PD services which caused repeated pages. this may be the cause of the flap.

SRE Lead: good catch. if it's dedup/duplicate paging we should silence the secondary PD integration until we confirm. priority: verify customer impact, then stop noisy pages.

oncall-bot: PagerDuty ack recorded by Alex P @ 1719001239. Incident assigned to: Alex P.

Alex P: quick mitigation — temporarily moved eu traffic away from node pool eu-a-3 where errors concentrated. rerouting command:
```
redwoodctl route update --pool eu-a-3 --drain --fallback-pool eu-b-1
```
Replaced prefix-caches to force KV warmup on fallback.

incident-bot: INFO automated-suppression applied: similar alerts from same signature will be throttled for 10m to avoid noise (rule id: noise-suppress-42)

Maya R: is there any persistent error in model runtime logs? i'm tailing /var/log/runtime/errors on eu-a-3

Alex P: nothing fatal in runtime logs. just a burst of connection resets to a backing redis proxy ~1719001175-1719001210. probable brief networking hiccup.

Emily S: verifying customer impact again — internal test harness shows requests recovered to normal by 1719001500. I don't see failed batches or degraded outputs in the last 10m.

SRE Lead: ok, sounds transient with low customer impact. action items: (1) follow up with network team about proxy resets, (2) add cross-region PD deduping rule, (3) tune noise-suppress-42 to 30m if we see repeats. @Maya R @Jordan K can one of you own the follow-ups?

Jordan K: i'll take (1) and (3). will open a ticket and ping netops.

Maya R: i'll take (2) — add dedup rules and test in staging. also will add a short postmortem note to the incident tracker.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert for service=redwood-runtime-eu auto-resolved at 1719001602 (incident closed, duration ~368s)

Alex P: handing off to next oncall in 28m. leaving notes: transient networking hiccup -> temporary reroute -> autoscale behaved as expected -> no customer tickets. escalate if you see reoccurrence.

oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: next_oncall=@Emily S at 1719003600. Please ack when you take over.

Emily S: acked for handoff. adding timeline and logs to the incident ticket. :thumbsup:

SRE Lead: nice quick mitigation. we'll treat this as a low-severity transient flap but follow up on deduping alert sources.

Alex P: closing thread from my side. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
